nodes.label: Unicode case-fold char-count divergence
nodes.norm_label: unicode case-fold char-count divergence
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c14-case-matching-corruption [ses_f1d0c30feffeY5Rb1TxHJ3dFer].md:L2602] `formatting.rs:6` and `formatting.rs:15`/`:18` call Unicode case mapping on **individually iterated chars** and `extend()` the result, so a 1-char input can legally become 2+ output chars. This is the whole bug, in three lines.

nodes.label: detect_case guards on byte length, so a non-ASCII single char reaches Uppercase
nodes.norm_label: detect_case guards on byte length, so a non-ascii single char reaches uppercase
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c14-case-matching-corruption [ses_f1d0c30feffeY5Rb1TxHJ3dFer].md:L2535] because `matching.rs:21` guards on **byte** length, `detect_case("A") == Original` (pinned by an existing test, `matching/tests.rs:118-119`) but `detect_case("É")` (1 char, 2 bytes) falls through to `matching.rs:24` and returns **`Uppercase`**. So non-ASCII single-character keywords reach the `Uppercase` branch where their ASCII counterparts do not.

nodes.label: Case folding can strand the cursor_offset computed on the expanded text
nodes.norm_label: case folding can strand the cursor_offset computed on the expanded text
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar-proyek-snipset/2026-09-27 - c14-case-matching-corruption [ses_f1d0c30feffeY5Rb1TxHJ3dFer].md:L2573] **Consequence:** whenever `Uppercase` or `TitleCase` is active and a multi-char case mapping is encountered **before** the cursor marker, the marker physically moves within `final_text` while `cursor_offset` keeps its old value, so the caret lands at the wrong position.
